raw_comment:
What do I notice?  I notice that this graph is showing the different patterns for droughts in the United States. The different colors represent the severity of droughts in each area. I notice that the most severe spots for droughts are aras not near the coast, like the north and south west. The darker the color, the moire prone the area is to droughts. I also notice that some of the areas near the coast are becoming more prone to droughts. 
What do I wonder? I wonder why parts of the country have a tendency to have more droughts, and other areas are a lot less likely to have a drought. Maybe this is because of the rainfall patterns, and which areas are more likely to have rain or snow. I also wonder why certain areas that tend to snow are still the most prone to droughts. 
How does this relate to you and your community? This relates to my community because in the past few months, New Jersey has become a threat for a drought. For some reason, it has been raining a lot less than normal. Due to these drought threats, fire pits and  bonfires are not allowed in my town. 
headline for the graph: droughts: how climate change is affecting the country.
